html: The Warriyangga, also written Wariangga, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Gascoyne region of Western Australia, in the inland country of the upper Lyons River. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Little is recorded about them. Their neighbours were the Tharrkari to the west, the Thiin and Jiwarli to the north and the Yinggarda to the southwest. Sheep stations took up the Gascoyne from the late 1800s.
